method: LTT/Bentkus risk control on inner OOF calibrated scores. S-zone error<=alpha=0.015, R-zone error<=beta=0.20 at delta=0.05; certified upper bound = inverted Bentkus. Baseline = empirical NPV/PPV thresholds. Audited S1 pooled, per-fold, out-of-site, cross-source; class-constant prevalence weights (Tibshirani 2019).
interpretation: R-zone certified: bound 0.1963 <= beta 0.2 (achieved 0.14342629482071714). S-zone NOT certifiable at alpha=0.015/delta=0.05: best achievable bound 0.0155 (at tS=0.022); the strict NPV>=98.5% certificate fails given the score distribution. Certified policy abstains from S (tS=None), U-zone 630->11617 (widens, as pre-registered). Out-of-site S violations 0/11; cross-source transfer in tables. The bound, not the point target, is the guarantee.
caveats: Patient grouping => effective n ~ patients; marginal split-conformal validity only, not i.i.d. R-zone bound is wide (~170 positives/fold). Prevalence-weighted certificate is approximate at an estimated user prevalence (Barber 2022 coverage-gap). Exchangeability breaks across labs — violations are a RESULT, motivating the per-lab prevalence slider.
supports: First risk-controlled triage application to BDQ resistance (to our knowledge); distribution-free abstention certificates re-weighted to lab prevalence.
